name: Scott Bessent
role: U.S. Secretary of the Treasury (2025–present); former hedge-fund manager
summary: Bessent is a Republican economic policymaker who favors extending and expanding tax cuts, financial deregulation, tariffs framed as trade rebalancing and industrial rebuilding, and fiscal restraint through spending cuts and growth. He supports Fed independence in principle while calling for review of the institution, and takes a hard line on China and Iran. He has said little publicly on most social and cultural questions.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Wants to re-privatize the economy and says government has crowded out the private sector, but also endorses industrial policy and doubts the invisible hand on resilience.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: At his confirmation hearing he opposed ending the 2017 tax cuts even for earners above $400,000 and said there is no income level at which they should lapse; he later praised the 2025 tax law.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Describes regulatory overreach and 'excessive regulation' as holding back growth and works to reduce regulation, especially of banks.

state-harmful.rationale: Calls for a right-sized government and a larger private sector but also assigns the state active roles in regulation, sanctions and Trump Accounts.

reduce-immigration.rationale: No stated position on immigration levels; remarks on unauthorised immigration are something nearby.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Wants the IMF and World Bank pulled back from mission creep and held to core mandates, though with expanded U.S. leadership in them; no stated wish for more power.

free-trade.rationale: Says access to cheap goods is not the essence of the American Dream and that the old trade system with persistent imbalances is unsustainable; says America First does not mean America alone.

nation-first.rationale: Frames policy as America First and says international institutions must ensure American resources serve American interests, while adding it does not mean acting alone.

open-borders.rationale: Praises the sealing of the border and says banks must not facilitate unlawful employment of unauthorized workers.

limit-growth.rationale: Calls growth the condition on which durable prosperity depends and sets growth targets.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Dismisses climate-focused sustainability and climate finance targets and says regulators' focus on climate risk was a distraction.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Applauded the World Bank's move to lift its ban on nuclear financing and wants all baseload technologies available; Wikipedia reports he backs expanding nuclear power.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Defends tariffs as a way to level the playing field, rebuild manufacturing and reward production over consumption.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Treats the unfashionable status of industrial policy as a past mistake and backs executive action on critical minerals, shipbuilding and pharmaceutical ingredients.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Describes building an 'ownership economy' and a new class of shareholders through Trump Accounts, with the Treasury seeding each child.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Warned of impending financial calamity from high spending and debt and says the U.S. must get its fiscal house in order; he also argues tax cuts raise growth.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Calls for cheap and plentiful energy, works with the energy and interior secretaries on energy security, and says gas and fossil energy suit most energy investment.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Backs state roles beyond defense and property protection, such as industrial policy, tariffs and seeding children's investment accounts.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Says security guarantees and open markets to allies continue while allies must step up their defense commitments.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Answered 'Of course' when asked whether the Fed should be independent of the president and said it should focus on monetary policy and low inflation; he has also called for a broad review of the Fed.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: No stated position on racial preferences in admissions or hiring; criticising DEI at the Fed is something nearby.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Says IMF lending should come in exchange for reforms and that the IMF should say no to countries that do not implement them.

notes: Most recent position wins. Only the pages cited were opened; the Senate Finance Committee hearing page and PDF, Michigan Advance and Fortune returned 403 or redirects, and no hearing transcript was read (hearing statements come from the AP report).
